source.document: No external published source exists for these metrics — confirmed by fetching and text-searching the DMO's own pinned price/yield methodology document ("Formulae for Calculating Gilt Prices from Yields", 4th ed., 18 Dec 2024, M-UK-01), which covers only price/yield conversion, dividend calculation, and accrued interest. FIN-001 §11 anticipates this: modified duration has 'no universal denominator hard-coded', and convexity's bump size/formula are 'specification-owned'.
source.inputs_reused_from: app/modules/calculation/specs/gilt_price_yield_v1/golden/v1/corpus.json price_from_yield_cases (the same 8 real DMO-sourced bond scenarios — bond terms and yields are genuine DMO worked-example inputs, not invented).
source.expected_values_derivation: expected_macaulay_duration/expected_modified_duration/expected_dv01/expected_convexity were computed from gilt_risk_metrics_v1's own analytical (shadow) implementation — a time-weighted discrete cash-flow present-value sum, re-derived from calculus (dP/dy = -v*sum(t_k*PV_k), etc.) and documented in shadow_implementation.py's own docstring. This is the closest available thing to ground truth given no external source exists, but it is honestly NOT an independently-published reference the way gilt_price_yield_v1's DMO worked examples are — see FIN-001 §26 FIN-O3 (Product+Methodology sign-off on the customer-facing definition/release-tier), which this corpus does not resolve. This golden test therefore checks (a) the analytical implementation reproduces its own frozen historical values (catches future regressions), and (b) the numerical bump-and-reprice production implementation agrees with those values within a tolerance wide enough to absorb its inherent finite-difference truncation error (measured empirically at roughly 1e-9 to 1e-5 depending on metric across these 8 cases), not an exact match.
